acts.d: Attackers brute force passwords for the RDP service
Attackers purchased stolen credentials from the black market for the victim's RDP service
Attacker exploited a vulnerability in the Windows COM Aggregate Marshaler
Attackers use GPO to move laterally
Attackers use PowerShell to move laterally
Attackers used GPO to execute Microsoft Installer
Attackers install a 122MB crafted, unsigned MSI package from the remote web server
Attackers run an executable, batch file, and support files
Batch file terminates many processes/servers and remote management software, closes opened files, and disables AntiVirus software
The batch file deletes volume shadow copies (so older unencrypted versions of files cannot be restored)
Attackers check for locale information. If the machine’s default language matches one on the CIS list, the ransomware process is terminated with the “666” exit code.
The attacker deploys a VirtualBox VM and loads a Windows XP image
The VM image maps all local drives as read/writable into the virtual machine. This allows the ransomware process running inside the VM to encrypt all files.
The ransomware steals files and uploads them to one or more servers in case the victim refuses to pay the ransom
Attackers protect the ransomware code with junk code and encryption

Ragnar Locker begins the encryption process in 64 simultaneous threads. The encrypted file contains the encrypted Salsa20 key data (40+32 bytes) with the signature ‘_RAGNAR_’ added to the footer at the very end.
